meta.archiveNote: UNREACHABLE at runtime, independent of auth/middleware. Next.js App Router treats any path segment starting with an underscore as a private folder (https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/routing/colocation#private-folders) and excludes it from route generation entirely. So app/api/_archive/**/route.js files never become live endpoints — a request to /api/_archive/anything 404s before middleware.js or next.config.js are even consulted for that path. Confirmed by reading next.config.js (no rewrites() or redirects() entry references '_archive') and middleware.js in full (zero string matches for '_archive'; its matcher config only lists '/api/:path*' plus specific pages, and none of the demo-mode dispatch tables, PUBLIC_ROUTES, or hosted-public-path checks mention _archive). scripts/lib/route-sql-guard.mjs explicitly skips the '_archive' directory when walking route files, confirming the team already treats it as inert/excluded tooling-side. Net effect: these 48 archived route files are dead code from a routing standpoint — the handlers themselves are syntactically intact and mostly still reference live schema tables (verified goals, milestones, ideas, contacts, interactions, agent_messages, message_threads, shared_docs, context_points, context_entries, calendar_events, snippets, user_observations/preferences/moods/approaches, notification_preferences, workflows, executions, scheduled_jobs, agent_pairings, agent_identities, content, health_snapshots, entities, topics, and feedback all still exist in schema/schema.js), but none of that matters because the folder is never mounted as a route. Un-archiving (renaming _archive -> something routable) would make most of them functional again since they read live tables.

items.name: POST /api/approvals/{actionId}/grant
items.purpose: Mint a scoped allow_grant from an approval card ("Allow, don't ask again") and report which pending approvals it covers. Approves NOTHING itself: the caller releases the returned release_ids over POST /api/approvals/{actionId}, so there stays exactly one approval path carrying one audit / webhook / calibration chain.

items.errors: 403 Admin access required / APPROVER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED; 403 GRANT_RISK_CEILING (risk_score >= 70 — a grant could not cover it anyway); 403 GRANT_REFUSED_BY_POLICY (a matched gating rule is marked ungrantable); 400 UNSCOPED_GRANT_REJECTED (the action's shape has no target prefix — F1, governance gap audit 2026-08-05); 400 INVALID_TTL; 400 action not pending_approval; 404 Action not found

items.name: GET /api/calibration/controller
items.purpose: Snapshot of the calibrated interruption controller (theory: docs/architecture/governance-core-theory.md §1, UI: /policies#calibration): settings (mode, target rate α), calibrated state (θ, labeled benign/denied counts split into live and retrospective warn_review labels, long-run + windowed observed false-interruption rate), top per-agent e-process alarms, recent adjudication events, and the org's active risk_threshold policies for θ-vs-policy context. Also reports labeled_live, relief_min_live_labels, and active_eligible (true only after 7 straight days within target).

Which arms run is a human decision made here by click (MAINTAINER.md §3): 'relief' only removes interruptions (require_approval below the calibrated threshold becomes a recorded warn, never past the riskiest action the operator approved), 'active' also adds them. Neither reaches allow, touches a block, or edits a policy row.

items.name: GET /api/enforcement-liveness
items.purpose: Latest enforcement-liveness probe runs for the caller's org plus the derived surface state. The probe (hooks/enforcement_liveness_probe.py, auto-spawned by the SessionStart digest at most every 12h) drives a synthetic held action through the real PreToolUse hook seam and verdicts by whether the action executed — never by reading the decision ledger (the v4.72.1 lesson). Human surfaces: /setup#enforcement-liveness card and the global status bar posture tile.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware
items.response: { runs:[{id, org_id, source, verdict:'held'|'executed'|'unprovable', detail, hook:{installed, settings_path?, timeout_seconds?, effective_timer_ms?, overflowed?, mode?, exit_code?, cancelled?}, witness:{path, executed}, decision, checks:[{id,title,status:'pass'|'fail'|'info',detail?,durationMs?}], started_at, finished_at, created_at}], stale_after_ms: 86400000, state:'holding'|'stale'|'broken' }
items.errors: 400 invalid limit; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise
items.gotchas: state derives from the latest run and the 24h staleness window: no run within 24h renders 'stale' (a probe that silently stopped running is itself the v4.72.1 failure shape and must not render green); verdict 'executed' or 'unprovable' renders 'broken'. Probe runs land in enforcement_liveness_runs only — never action_records/guard_decisions (live-canary precedent).

items.name: POST /api/enforcement-liveness
items.purpose: Files an enforcement-liveness probe verdict. Called by hooks/enforcement_liveness_probe.py after it runs the installed pretool hook under harness-faithful timeout semantics (timeout is SECONDS; seconds*1000 past int32 overflows the harness timer and cancels the hook fail-open) and observes the witness.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware

inputs.body.hook: object, required — installed (boolean, required) + whitelisted diagnostics (settings_path, timeout_seconds, effective_timer_ms, overflowed, mode, exit_code, cancelled)
inputs.body.checks: array 1-50 of {id, title, status pass|fail|info, detail?, durationMs?}, required
inputs.body.decision: string ≤200, optional — recorded guard decision, diagnosis only

items.response: 201 { id } (elr_-prefixed)
items.errors: 400 per-field validation errors naming the field; apiErrorResponse-shaped error otherwise
items.gotchas: Inserting prunes the org's runs older than 30 days in the same call (retention rides along, no cron). Unknown hook fields are dropped, wrong-typed known fields are rejected. Runs are structurally excluded from posture scoring, calibration mining, and funnel truth by never touching the action/guard ledgers.

items.name: GET /api/guard

Guard has an internal evaluation deadline; on timeout or inte…

items.purpose: List guardrail (guard) decisions for a dashboard-style view, parsing stored JSON columns and joining aggregate stats in one call.

items.name: GET /api/halt
items.purpose: Returns the org's kill-switch (org halt) state.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.response: { halt: { halted: boolean, actor: string|null, reason: string|null, at: string|null } }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; standard apiErrorResponse on failure
items.gotchas: State is stored as a JSON-encoded settings row under key DASHCLAW_ORG_HALT, category 'general'.

items.name: POST /api/halt
items.purpose: Sets or clears the org-wide kill switch; while halted, every guard evaluation for the org immediately blocks (still recorded/audited).
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.response: { ok: true, halt: { halted, actor, reason, at } }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 400 if halted is not a boolean; standard apiErrorResponse on failure
items.gotchas: Invalidates the guard settings cache eagerly (invalidateGuardSettingsCache) so the switch takes effect immediately rather than after the ~30s guard cache TTL; writes an activity_logs audit row (org.halted / org.resumed); actor uses real user id, falling back to 'admin'.

items.name: GET /api/approval-pause
items.purpose: Reports whether the org is currently skipping approval prompts, and the windows an admin may choose.
items.auth: any org member (read). Deliberately not admin-gated: everyone reading /approvals needs to know whether that inbox is the whole picture.
items.response: { pause: { active, until, actor, reason, at, remaining_seconds }, window_hours: [1,4,8,24] }
items.errors: standard apiErrorResponse on failure
items.gotchas: Expiry is decided on READ against the stored absolute `until`, so an elapsed pause reports inactive with no write, cron or reaper involved.

items.name: POST /api/approval-pause
items.purpose: Starts (or extends) the approval pause. While it is live, a require_approval verdict proceeds instead of waiting for a human — blocks are untouched and an `ungrantable` gate still interrupts.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.response: { ok: true, pause: { active, until, actor, reason, at, remaining_seconds } }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 400 if hours is not one of the allowed windows; standard apiErrorResponse on failure
items.gotchas: Windows are an allowlist, not a free number: an unbounded pause is the June 2026 'all policies off for 18 days' outage with a nicer label. Stores an absolute deadline in a JSON settings row under DASHCLAW_APPROVAL_PAUSE, category 'general' (so the guard hot path reads it on its existing category-general query), and invalidates the guard settings cache eagerly. Policy rows are never modified, so expiry restores the exact prior posture. Writes an activity_logs row (org.approvals_paused).

items.name: DELETE /api/approval-pause
items.purpose: Resumes asking for approvals immediately.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.response: { ok: true, pause: { active: false, ... } }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; standard apiErrorResponse on failure
items.gotchas: Idempotent — clearing an absent or already-expired pause succeeds. Writes an expired marker rather than deleting the row, so the activity log keeps who resumed. Invalidates the guard settings cache eagerly because resuming governance is a safety action and must not lag a warm instance. Writes an activity_logs row (org.approvals_resumed).

items.purpose: Claimability preview for the /claim page (v5.13 G2 product half): resolves the browser's anonymous trial cookie to its org and reports whether it can be claimed, whether the caller is signed in, and whether their current workspace can be left behind.

items.purpose: Claim the browser's anonymous trial workspace for the signed-in user (v5.13): atomically stamps claimed_at/claimed_by_user_id, clears trial_ends_at (the org stops expiring), renames the org after the owner, rebinds the user as admin, discards the empty auto-minted personal org, and clears the trial cookie.

items.response: { claimed: true, org_id } (adds recovered: true when finishing a previously crashed claim).
items.errors: 404 off-hosted; 400 no_trial_session; 401 sign_in_required; 409 already_claimed|expired|not_trial|not_claimable|current_workspace_not_empty.
items.gotchas: A user whose account already owns a workspace with history gets 409 current_workspace_not_empty - claiming moves the account, it never merges or discards existing work. Outstanding anonymous trial cookies for a claimed org stop resolving within the middleware's 60s org cache.

items.name: GET /api/integrations/health
items.purpose: Returns the last-checked health status for each configured integration provider.
items.auth: x-api-key (default-deny middleware); no role check
items.response: { health: { [provider]: { status, message, checked_at } } }
items.errors: 500 on failure
items.gotchas: Read-only snapshot of stored rows — does not trigger a fresh check (use the refresh route for that).

items.name: POST /api/integrations/health/refresh
items.purpose: Runs an on-demand health check across all configured integrations, upserts results, fires alerts on status transitions, and returns the refreshed health map. Free-tier alternative to the Bearer-authed cron endpoint.
items.auth: admin (getOrgRole === 'admin')
items.response: { checked: number, alerts: number, health: { [provider]: { status, message, checked_at } } }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 500 on failure
items.gotchas: maxDuration 60s; skips providers with status 'not_configured'; alerts only fire for providers whose status actually changed (fireHealthChangeAlerts); prev_status may be null for a fresh row.

items.name: GET /api/integrity/jwks
items.purpose: Serves the public JWKS used to independently re-verify DashClaw-issued proof receipts and signed compliance bundles.
items.auth: public (listed in middleware PUBLIC_ROUTES; also aliased at /.well-known/jwks.json via next.config rewrite)
items.response: { keys: [...] } (standard JWKS shape, public halves only — never includes the `d` private member)
items.errors: Never returns 500 — on internal failure it falls back to { keys: [] } with status 200
items.gotchas: Cache-Control is 'public, max-age=300' only when keys are non-empty; an empty key set is served with 'no-store' so a pre-key-generation fetch never gets pinned at the edge.

items.name: POST /api/integrity/verify
items.purpose: Independently re-verifies a proof receipt or signed compliance bundle against the instance's published JWKS. Stateless — does not look up the original record.
items.auth: public (listed in middleware PUBLIC_ROUTES)
items.response: receipt: { ok: boolean, kid?, reason? }; bundle: verifyBundle result which also echoes prevBundleHash
items.errors: 400 if neither receipt nor bundle provided; never a true 500 — internal errors return 200 { ok:false, reason:'verification_error' } (fail-closed as a non-verification, not a server error)
items.gotchas: For receipts, tries the key whose kid matches the receipt signature first, then falls back to trying every published key; verifying a full bundle chain requires walking successive prevBundleHash links yourself.

items.name: POST /api/internal/resolve-key
items.purpose: Internal bridge used by edge middleware to resolve an API key hash to org/role on self-host deployments with a non-Neon (TCP-only) Postgres, since the edge Neon HTTP driver can't reach it.
items.auth: internal (x-internal-auth header must timing-safe match DASHCLAW_API_KEY, the instance operator key; middleware attaches this on the internal hop and nothing external can forge it)
items.response: { resolved: { keyId, orgId, role, hostedMode, trialEndsAt, trialActionCap, trialActionsUsed } | null, code? }
items.errors: 404 if not self-host mode or if DATABASE_URL is a Neon URL (route is a no-op everywhere else); 401 if x-internal-auth missing/invalid or DASHCLAW_API_KEY unset; 400 if keyHash missing; 500 on transient DB failure (with Postgres error `code` included…
items.gotchas: Deliberately 404s on Neon/hosted so it can never become a hash->org lookup oracle in those environments, even though the path itself is in middleware's PUBLIC_ROUTES; fires a non-blocking touchKeyLastUsed update on successful resolution.

items.name: GET /api/live-canary
items.purpose: Return the org's most recent live-host canary run(s) — production probe results from the hourly GitHub Actions cron.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.response: { runs: Array<live_canary_runs row> }
items.errors: 400 'invalid limit: expected an integer between 1 and 20'; apiErrorResponse-shaped error on DB failure
items.gotchas: Read side of a write-only-by-cron feature; runs never touch action/guard ledgers so they're invisible to posture scoring/calibration.

items.name: POST /api/live-canary
items.purpose: Record a live-host canary run verdict (production probe results) filed by the hourly GitHub Actions cron script.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi

inputs.body.checks: array of 1-50 {id, title, status:'pass'|'fail', detail?, target?, durationMs?}, required

items.response: 201 { id: string }
items.errors: 400 'invalid <field>: <reason>' for any malformed body/check field; apiErrorResponse on DB failure
items.gotchas: Deliberately never writes to action_records or guard_decisions — keeps canary traffic invisible to posture/calibration by design.

items.name: POST /api/marketing/event
items.purpose: Record anonymous marketing-funnel telemetry events (allowlisted event names) to Redis for the marketing site.
items.auth: public — listed in middleware.js PUBLIC_ROUTES ('/api/marketing'); no API key or session required

inputs.body.event: string, required, must be one of: marketing_hero_cta_clicked, marketing_github_clicked, marketing_demo_evaluated, marketing_self_host_visited, marketing_proof_visited, marketing_vs_section_viewed
inputs.body.properties: flat object, optional, max 8 keys, each string value ≤200 bytes; number/boolean allowed

items.response: 202 { ok: true } — always, regardless of whether Redis actually persisted
items.errors: 400 'invalid_json'; 400 'unknown_event'; 400 with properties validation error string
items.gotchas: No PII/cookies/third-party trackers; response is intentionally uninformative about Redis persistence so clients can't infer server config; rate limit + 2MB body cap still apply via standard middleware path; ip read from x-client-ip header set by middleware, not directly from the request.

items.name: POST /api/mcp
items.purpose: Streamable-HTTP MCP protocol endpoint (JSON-RPC 2.0): initialize, tools/list, tools/call, resources/list, resources/read, ping — proxies to DashClawClient/tool+resource handlers.
items.auth: x-api-key (Managed Agents/remote MCP hosts) OR OAuth Bearer token (Claude custom connector, via /api/oauth flow) — both handled by middleware's authenticateProtectedApi/handleBearerAuth; unauthentica…

inputs.body.params: object, method-specific (e.g. { name, arguments } for tools/call; { uri } for resources/read)

items.response: JSON-RPC 2.0 frame: { jsonrpc: '2.0', id, result } (or { error: {code, message} }); notifications/initialized returns 204 No Content per spec
items.errors: -32602 'Unknown tool'/'Unknown resource'; -32601 'Method not found'; -32603 'Internal error' (wrapped as HTTP 500); tool-call errors return isError:true content instead of throwing
items.gotchas: OAuth Bearer callers get a hardcoded agentId 'claude-desktop' identity (not caller-chosen) — a governance primitive, not a bug; instanceOrigin() self-callback resolution deliberately avoids trusting a spoofed Host header (SSRF/credential-exfil defense) — prefers DASHCLAW_URL then VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL then request Host.

items.name: GET /api/oauth/authorize
items.purpose: OAuth 2.1 authorization endpoint: validates PKCE/client/redirect_uri, requires a logged-in browser session, and renders a minimal HTML consent page.
items.auth: NextAuth session cookie (getToken) — NOT x-api-key; unauthenticated requests redirect to /login. Route itself is public per middleware (/api/oauth prefix self-authenticates)

inputs.query.client_id: string, required — must resolve via DCR-registered client
inputs.query.redirect_uri: string, required — must be in the client's registered redirect_uris

items.response: 200 text/html consent page with a POST-back form (CSP: form-action restricted to self + client's callback origin), or 302 redirect to /login if no session
items.errors: 400 unsupported_response_type / invalid_request (missing PKCE/client/redirect) / invalid_client / invalid_redirect_uri (JSON body)
items.gotchas: This is the Claude custom-connector OAuth AS, not a normal API route — human must have an active NextAuth or local-admin session to reach consent.

items.name: POST /api/oauth/authorize
items.purpose: Consent-page submission: issues a short-lived authorization code bound to the session's org/user and the validated PKCE challenge.
items.auth: NextAuth session cookie (getToken) required; same-origin CSRF check (Origin/Referer must match Host)

inputs.query.same params as GET: response_type, client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, code_challenge_method, state, scope

items.response: 303 redirect to redirect_uri with ?code=<opaque 'oac' token>&state=<state>
items.errors: 403 'invalid_request'/cross-origin rejected; 401 'login_required'; 400 same validation errors as GET
items.gotchas: Auth code TTL is 5 minutes; agentId hardcoded to 'claude-desktop' on the stored auth_codes row; 303 (not 307) used deliberately so the browser GETs the callback instead of re-POSTing.

items.name: GET /api/oauth/metadata/authorization-server
items.purpose: RFC 8414 OAuth Authorization Server Metadata discovery document.
items.auth: public (no auth) — OAuth discovery must be reachable unauthenticated
items.response: { issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, registration_endpoint, response_types_supported: ['code'], grant_types_supported: ['authorization_code','refresh_token'], code_challenge_methods_supported: ['S256'], token_endpoint_auth_methods_supported: ['none'], scopes_supported: ['governance:read','governance:write'] }
items.errors: none — always 200
items.gotchas: issuerBase() prefers DASHCLAW_URL, then falls back to request Host — self-host operators behind a proxy that forwards an arbitrary Host should set DASHCLAW_URL explicitly; aliased at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server via middleware+next.config rewrite.

items.name: GET /api/oauth/metadata/protected-resource
items.purpose: RFC 9728 OAuth Protected Resource Metadata document, identifying /api/mcp as the protected resource.
items.auth: public (no auth)
items.response: { resource: '<base>/api/mcp', authorization_servers: ['<base>'] }
items.errors: none — always 200
items.gotchas: Aliased at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource; used by mcpAuthChallenge's WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata pointer.

items.name: POST /api/oauth/register
items.purpose: OAuth Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) — open registration, no auth required, for MCP/connector clients.
items.auth: public — deliberately open (DCR is designed to be), but redirect_uri is strictly validated to prevent open-redirect abuse

inputs.body.redirect_uris: array of strings, required, non-empty after filtering — each must be an absolute https URI (no fragment); http allowed only for localhost/127.0.0.1 outside production

items.response: 201 { client_id, client_id_issued_at, redirect_uris, grant_types: ['authorization_code','refresh_token'], token_endpoint_auth_method: 'none' }
items.errors: 400 'invalid_redirect_uri' if no valid redirect_uris survive filtering
items.gotchas: Any caller can register a client (no auth) — this is intentional per the OAuth DCR spec, but the redirect_uri allowlist is the load-bearing security control (prevents auth-code harvesting via an attacker-registered callback).

items.name: POST /api/oauth/token
items.purpose: OAuth token endpoint — exchanges an authorization_code (with PKCE verifier) or refresh_token for an access/refresh token pair.
items.auth: public (no bearer/api-key auth) — token endpoint self-authenticates via the code/PKCE verifier or refresh token itself; token_endpoint_auth_method is 'none' (public client)

inputs.body: application/x-www-form-urlencoded: grant_type ('authorization_code'|'refresh_token'), plus for authorization_code: code, redirect_uri, code_verifier, client_id; for refresh_token: refresh_token

items.response: { access_token, token_type: 'Bearer', expires_in: 3600, refresh_token, scope }
items.errors: 400 'invalid_request' (missing fields); 400 'invalid_grant' (unknown/expired/replayed code, client/redirect mismatch, wrong PKCE method, failed PKCE verify, bad refresh token); 400 'unsupported_grant_type'
items.gotchas: Access tokens expire in 1 hour; auth codes are single-use (consumeAuthCode) and bound to client_id+redirect_uri+S256 PKCE only — no plain challenge ever accepted even defensively.

items.name: GET /api/operations/summary
items.purpose: Aggregate operations dashboard summary: decision throughput, latency percentiles, approval backlog, workflow health, and capability health counts.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi
items.response: { throughput: {last_1h, last_24h}, latency: {p50_ms, p95_ms}, approval_backlog: {pending_count, oldest_minutes, avg_wait_minutes}, workflows: {running, failed_24h, completed_24h, avg_duration_ms}, capabilities: {healthy, degraded, failing, untested} }
items.errors: apiErrorResponse-shaped error on failure
items.gotchas: Each of the 5 sub-queries is individually wrapped in a safe() catch that degrades to a single empty-object row on failure, so one bad query zeroes only its own card, not the whole response; latency uses true PERCENTILE_CONT p50/p95 (a prior bug used AVG/MAX mislabeled as p50/p95).

items.name: GET /api/orgs
items.purpose: List organizations. In practice returns only the caller's own org (with its active API key count) — not a global org list.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin'.
items.response: { organizations: [...] } — rows from listOrgWithActiveKeys scoped to the caller's org_id only (security note in code: intentionally not a cross-tenant list).
items.errors: 403 Forbidden if role !== admin; 500 on unexpected DB error.
items.gotchas: Despite the name/route, this never returns other orgs — it always filters by the caller's own org_id server-side, regardless of query params.

items.name: POST /api/orgs
items.purpose: Create a new organization and mint its first admin API key.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin'. Additionally blocked for hosted-trial principals via denyTrialPrincipal (trial admins ca…
items.response: 201 { organization: {...row, plan:'free'}, api_key: { id, key (raw, shown once), prefix, role:'admin', warning } }
items.errors: 403 if not admin or trial principal denied; 400 if name/slug missing or invalid; 409 if slug already exists (unique/duplicate DB error); 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: 'plan' in the request body is ignored — always forced to 'free' server-side (upgrades only via Stripe webhooks). Default scoring/risk profile data is seeded asynchronously (fire-and-forget) after org creation, so a seed failure won't fail the request but data may lag briefly. The returned api_key.key is the only time the raw key is ever shown.

items.name: GET /api/orgs/{orgId}
items.purpose: Fetch details for a single organization, including its active API key count.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires admin role. Additionally the orgId path param must equal the caller's own org_id.

inputs.pathParams.orgId: string, must match caller's own org

items.response: { organization: {...row}, active_keys: number (parsed from countActiveKeys) }
items.errors: 403 if not admin, or if orgId !== caller's org (cross-tenant access blocked); 404 if org not found; 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: Cannot be used to view any other org — enforced by direct orgId===callerOrgId comparison, not just a WHERE clause.

items.name: PATCH /api/orgs/{orgId}
items.purpose: Update an organization's name.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires admin role; orgId path param must equal caller's own org_id.

inputs.body.name: string, optional; if provided must be non-empty, <=256 chars

items.response: { organization: {...updated row} }
items.errors: 403 if not admin or cross-tenant; 404 if org not found; 400 if name invalid; 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: 'plan' is intentionally excluded from this endpoint — plan changes only happen via Stripe webhooks or an internal billing service, never via this PATCH.

items.name: DELETE /api/orgs/{orgId}/keys
items.purpose: Revoke an API key by id.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires admin role; orgId path param must equal caller's own org_id.

inputs.query.id: string, required, the key_id to revoke

items.response: { success: true, revoked: keyId }
items.errors: 403 if not admin or cross-tenant; 400 if id query param missing; 404 if key not found (for this org); 409 if key already revoked; 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: Revocation is scoped to (keyId, orgId) — cannot revoke another org's key even by guessing its id.

items.name: GET /api/orgs/{orgId}/keys
items.purpose: List API keys for an org (prefix only, never the hash/secret).
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires admin role; orgId path param must equal caller's own org_id.
items.response: { keys: [...] } — each key includes id/prefix/label/role/created_at/revoked_at etc, never the raw key or hash.
items.errors: 403 if not admin or cross-tenant; 404 if org not found; 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: None beyond standard org-scoping checks.

items.name: POST /api/orgs/{orgId}/keys
items.purpose: Generate a new API key for an org.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires admin role; orgId path param must equal caller's own org_id.

inputs.body.label: string, optional, default 'API Key', <=256 chars
inputs.body.role: string, optional, default 'member', one of admin|member|readonly

items.response: 201 { key: { id, key (raw, shown once), prefix, label, role, warning } }
items.errors: 403 if not admin or cross-tenant; 404 if org not found; 400 if label too long or role invalid; 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: Raw key format is `oc_live_{32 hex chars}`, hashed via sha256 before storage; only the prefix (first 8 chars) and hash are persisted. The raw key is returned exactly once.

items.name: GET /api/usage
items.purpose: Read-only per-org metering report (hosted paid tier G4): current-period governed/blocked action counts from the usage_rollups table, seats (human users + active API keys), trial cap state, and up to 12 months of history. Measurement only - nothing enforces off these numbers.
items.auth: API key or dashboard session; scoped to the caller org via x-org-id (middleware-resolved, never client-trusted).
items.response: { org_id, period: "YYYY-MM", governed_actions: number, blocked_actions: number, seats: { users, active_api_keys }, plan, hosted_mode, trial: { action_cap, actions_used } | null, history: [{ period, governed_actions, blocked_actions, updated_at }], lastUpdated }
items.errors: 500 { error: "Failed to fetch usage" }
items.gotchas: Counters come from usage_rollups, maintained inline by createActionRecord (both creation paths share it) - not a live COUNT over action_records. Rebuild/seed history with scripts/backfill-usage-rollups.mjs. Rendered by the /usage dashboard page.

items.name: GET /api/team/invites
items.purpose: The /team page's data source (v5.13 seats): the org, its members (seats), and pending email-matched invites in one response.
items.auth: Signed-in human org admin only (usr_ principal + admin role). Agent keys, the operator sentinel, and anonymous trial cookies are refused.
items.response: { org: { id, name, slug, plan }, members: [{ id, email, name, image, role, created_at, last_login_at }], invites: [{ id, email, role, createdAt, expiresAt, expired }] }
items.errors: 403 for every non-human-admin principal.
items.gotchas: Deliberately NOT gated by denyTrialPrincipal - that helper refuses every hosted_mode org, and a claimed org (hosted_mode + claimed_at) is exactly who manages seats.

items.name: POST /api/team/invites
items.purpose: Record an email-matched invite (v5.13): when the invited address signs in for the first time, the signIn callback binds that user into this org with the invited role instead of minting a personal workspace. No invite email is sent and no join link exists.
items.auth: Signed-in human org admin only.
items.response: 201 { invite: { id, email, role, expiresAt } } - email normalized to lowercase, 14-day expiry.
items.errors: 400 invalid_email|invalid_role or unparseable JSON; 409 already_member|already_invited; 403 non-admin.
items.gotchas: Invites bind at FIRST sign-in only - a returning user with a pending invite is never moved. One live invite per (org, address) via a partial unique index; accepted rows remain as audit history.

items.name: DELETE /api/team/invites
items.purpose: Revoke a pending invite before it is accepted (v5.13 seats).
items.auth: Signed-in human org admin only.
items.response: { revoked: true }
items.errors: 400 missing invite_id or unparseable JSON; 404 when the invite is unknown or already accepted; 403 non-admin.
items.gotchas: Accepted invites cannot be revoked (they are history, and the member already exists) - removing a member is a different, not-yet-built operation.

items.name: POST /api/billing/checkout
items.purpose: Start a Stripe subscription Checkout Session for the caller's org (v5.14 hosted paid tier). Plans: indie ($49/mo) and team ($199/mo) per docs/decisions/2026-08-09-hosted-paid-tier.md. Creates and stores the org's Stripe customer on first use (first-writer-wins).
items.auth: Signed-in human org admin only (usr_ principal + admin role). On hosted the org must be CLAIMED - you cannot bill an anonymous trial cookie.
items.response: { url } - the Stripe-hosted Checkout URL; the browser navigates there.
items.errors: 501 BILLING_NOT_CONFIGURED when Stripe env is absent (self-host answers honestly); 400 UNKNOWN_PLAN or bad JSON; 403 non-human-admin; 404 unknown org; 409 claim_required for unclaimed hosted orgs.
items.gotchas: Plan activation happens via the webhook, not the redirect - the success_url banner on /settings?tab=billing is cosmetic until checkout.session.completed lands. Success/cancel land on /settings?tab=billing&billing=success|canceled.

items.name: GET /api/billing/portal
items.purpose: Open a Stripe customer portal session for the org's stored customer (manage payment method, cancel, invoices).
items.auth: Signed-in human org admin only.
items.response: { url } - the Stripe-hosted portal URL.
items.errors: 501 BILLING_NOT_CONFIGURED; 400 NO_CUSTOMER when the org never checked out; 403 non-human-admin.
items.gotchas: Returns to /settings?tab=billing. Cancellations propagate back through customer.subscription.deleted on the webhook, which restores the free-tier action cap on hosted orgs.

items.name: POST /api/webhooks/stripe
items.purpose: Stripe event intake (v5.14): checkout.session.completed activates the plan and clears the trial cap; customer.subscription.updated maps price ids to plans (unknown price keeps the stored plan); customer.subscription.deleted returns the org to free and restores the free cap; invoice.payment_failed marks past_due.
items.auth: PUBLIC route - auth is the stripe-signature header verified over the RAW body against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET (Telegram-webhook pattern; registered in PUBLIC_ROUTES).

inputs.body: Raw Stripe event payload (never re-serialized before verification)

items.response: { received: true } - plus duplicate: true when the event id was already claimed.
items.errors: 501 BILLING_NOT_CONFIGURED; 400 on signature verification failure. Unknown orgs/subscriptions still 200 (Stripe retries are for transport failures, not data we chose not to store).
items.gotchas: Every event id is claimed exactly once through the stripe_webhook_events ledger (drizzle/0070) BEFORE its handler runs - replays and retries acknowledge without re-applying. The culled 2026 webhook had no such ledger.

items.name: GET /api/pairings
items.purpose: List agent identity-pairing requests for the org, filtered by status.
items.auth: operator/admin required (getOrgRole(request) must be 'admin'), plus base x-api-key/session/OAuth bearer auth
items.response: { pairings: Array<pairing row (includes public_key)> }
items.errors: 403 'Admin access required'; 500 'Failed to list pairings'
items.gotchas: Unlike GET-by-id, list does NOT strip public_key from the response.

items.name: POST /api/pairings
items.purpose: Create a new agent pairing request (device/agent enrollment) with a PEM public key, awaiting admin approval.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi — no admin role required to CREATE a pairing (only to approve/list/patch)

inputs.body.public_key: string, required — must be PEM format containing 'BEGIN PUBLIC KEY'/'END PUBLIC KEY'

items.response: { pairing: inserted row, pairing_url: '<origin>/pair/<id>' }
items.errors: 400 'agent_id is required'; 400 'public_key must be a PEM public key'; 500 'Failed to create pairing'
items.gotchas: Pairing TTL configurable via DASHCLAW_PAIRING_TTL_MINUTES env (default 15 min, min 1); id format pair_<uuid>.

items.name: GET /api/pairings/{pairingId}
items.purpose: Fetch a single pairing's status, auto-expiring it if past expires_at and still pending.
items.auth: x-api-key (or session/OAuth bearer) via middleware authenticateProtectedApi — no admin role required for GET
items.response: { pairing: {...row minus public_key} }
items.errors: 404 'Pairing not found'; 500 'Failed to fetch pairing'
items.gotchas: public_key is stripped from the response (non-admin callers don't need it); side effect: GET can flip status pending→expired in the DB if TTL has passed.

items.name: PATCH /api/pairings/{pairingId}
items.purpose: Update a pairing's status (pending/expired only — NOT approved) and/or permission_level.
items.auth: operator/admin required (getOrgRole must be 'admin')

inputs.body.status: optional, one of: pending|expired (rejects 'approved' with a hint to use the /approve route)

items.response: { pairing: updated row }
items.errors: 403 'Admin access required'; 400 'No update fields provided'; 400 invalid status (with hint for 'approved'); 400 invalid permission_level; 404 'Pairing not found'; 500 'Failed to update pairing'
items.gotchas: Cannot approve via PATCH by design — approval must go through POST /approve, which is the only path that also creates the agent_identities row.

items.name: POST /api/pairings/{pairingId}/approve
items.purpose: Approve a pending pairing: upserts the agent's verified identity (public key) and marks the pairing approved.
items.auth: operator/admin required (getOrgRole must be 'admin')
items.response: { identity: upserted agent_identities row }
items.errors: 403 'Admin access required'; 404 'Pairing not found'; 410 'Pairing expired' (also expires it in DB); 409 'Pairing is not pending (status=...)'; 500 'Failed to approve pairing'
items.gotchas: This is the ONLY route that writes agent_identities from a pairing — the sole trust-establishment path; order of ops is upsertIdentity then approvePairing (identity created even if the later approvePairing write were to fail, though not handled specially).

items.name: GET /api/plans
items.purpose: List preflight plans for the org (Preflight Plan Authorization, RFC 2026-07-06), optionally filtered by status or agent_id, newest first.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.
items.response: 200: { plans: [...plan_authorizations rows] } ordered by created_at DESC.
items.errors: 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: limit is floored at 1 as well as capped at 200 (R4) — a negative or zero limit never reaches the SQL LIMIT clause.

items.name: POST /api/plans
items.purpose: Submit a preflight plan of ordered steps for operator review — each step is dry-run through the real guard pipeline (simulate:true, side-effect-free) at submission time so the operator reviews a genuine preview verdict.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate — any authenticated agent can submit a plan.

inputs.body.agent_id: string, optional — resolved via resolveAgentIdentity (falls back to signed/verified identity)
inputs.body.steps: array, required, non-empty — each { action_type: string, step_goal: string, act?: object }

items.response: 201: { plan, steps: [...steps with preview_decision/preview_risk_score/preview_reasons] }
items.errors: 400 agent_id/declared_goal/steps missing or invalid, step exceeds the PLAN_MAX_STEPS cap (hard ceiling 25 — an org setting may only tighten it, never widen it); 409 too many pending plans (MAX_PENDING_PLANS=10, SQL-enforced with a TTL-aging window so a stale unreviewed plan cannot brick the cap); 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: Each step's preview runs against the RAW act as submitted, never the redacted display copy stored server-side — the preview verdict is advisory only; a grant applies only when the LIVE evaluation still lands on require_approval. created_by is stamped from the middleware-attributed principal for separation of duties (drizzle/0063) — the submitter cannot later approve their own plan.

items.name: GET /api/plans/{planId}
items.purpose: Agent-facing poll for a submitted plan's review state, including per-step grant status.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.
items.response: 200: { plan, steps }
items.errors: 404 Plan not found; 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: No admin gate — any credential for the org can read a plan's status, matching the agent-poll use case (waitForPlanReview in the SDK).

items.name: POST /api/plans/{planId}
items.purpose: Operator verdict on a submitted plan — approve (optionally with per-step overrides), deny, or revoke — mirroring the approvals gate's admin + attributable-principal auth pattern.
items.auth: admin role required (getOrgRole(request) === 'admin') plus an attributable principal (x-user-id); 403 APPROVER_IDENTITY_REQUIRED if unattributed.

inputs.body.step_overrides: object, optional — { [stepId]: 'approve'|'deny' }, only honored on verdict=approve

items.response: 200: { plan, steps }
items.errors: 400 invalid verdict, invalid step_overrides value; 403 admin required, unattributed reviewer, SELF_APPROVAL_FORBIDDEN (the submitting principal cannot approve its own plan — drizzle/0063, exempts 'operator'); 404 plan not found or not reviewable in its current status; 500 Internal server error; SoD also covers deny and lifting a denial (a second principal or 'operator' required), and principal-less (NULL created_by) rows are operator-only
items.gotchas: The self-approval gate only applies to verdict=approve — denying or revoking your own plan is allowed. Approval TTL is clamped by PLAN_GRANT_TTL_MAX_MINUTES (may only tighten the 480-minute hard ceiling, never widen it). Denied steps block the matching action org-wide (not scoped to the submitting agent_id) until the plan's TTL expires.

items.name: POST /api/plans/{planId}/attest
items.purpose: Run-start attestation seam (Plan Attestation, v5.28.0): an unattended runner posts the plan_hash it is about to act under and gets a yes/no before its first model call, proving the pinned plan is still approved, unexpired and unrevoked.
items.auth: Agent-facing: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id (or session cookie), the same credential the GET poll uses. Deliberately NOT the admin + attributable-principal auth an operator verdict requires -- attesting is a read of one’s own authority, not a grant of it.

inputs.body.plan_hash: string, required -- the content hash pinned at submission

items.response: 200: { ok: true, plan_id, plan_hash, expires_at, steps_remaining }
items.errors: 400 plan_hash is required; 403 { ok: false, reason } with reason one of not_approved | expired | revoked | hash_mismatch; 404 { ok: false, reason: 'not_found' }; 500 Internal server error
items.gotchas: The stored hash is never echoed back on a mismatch -- returning it would hand a caller holding a stale or forged plan the exact digest needed to forge a matching attestation. Every call is journaled on BOTH arms (attest_count, attested_at, last_attest_result), so repeated attestation against a revoked or drifted plan shows up in the operator log and on the approvals plan card.

items.name: DELETE /api/policies
items.purpose: Delete one policy or bulk-delete multiple policies by id.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; requires admin role (403 otherwise).

inputs.query.id: string, optional — single policy id to delete
inputs.query.ids: comma-separated string, optional — bulk delete (?id and ?ids are mutually available; ids takes precedence when present)

items.response: Bulk: { deleted: number, ids: string[] }. Single: { deleted: true, id: string }.
items.errors: 400 neither id nor ids provided, or ids parses to an empty list; 404 (single mode) policy not found; 500 other.
items.gotchas: Deletion goes through deletePoliciesByIds repository (scoped to org_id). Publishes one EVENTS.POLICY_UPDATED (change_type: 'deleted') per deleted row and invalidates the guard cache once.

items.name: GET /api/policies
items.purpose: List guard policies for the org, optionally filtered to those that apply to a given agent.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; no admin gate.

inputs.query.agent_id: string, optional — when set, filters to policies with null/empty agent_ids (all agents) or agent_ids containing this id

items.response: { policies: GuardPolicyRow[] } — full guard_policies rows ordered by created_at DESC
items.errors: Standard apiErrorResponse (500) on DB failure; malformed agent_ids JSON on a row is treated as matching all agents (fail-open).
items.gotchas: In demo-org context, middleware intercepts this route entirely and returns fixture data (demoFixtureRoute(demoPolicies)) before the handler runs.

items.name: PATCH /api/policies
items.purpose: Update an existing guard policy's name, rules, active flag, or agent scoping.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; requires admin role (403 otherwise).

inputs.body.id: string, required — policy id to update
inputs.body.name: string, optional
inputs.body.rules: string or object, optional — re-validated via validatePolicy against the policy's existing (or body-supplied) policy_type before the UPDATE runs
inputs.body.policy_type: string, optional — only used to pick the validator when rules changes; not itself persisted by this route's SET clause
inputs.body.agent_ids: array/string or null, optional (checked via !== undefined so null clears scoping)

items.response: { policy: GuardPolicyRow } (the updated row via RETURNING *)
items.errors: 400 missing id / no fields to update / rules validation failed; 404 policy not found in org (checked explicitly before validating+writing rules, and again after the UPDATE); 500 other.
items.gotchas: Builds a dynamic parameterized SET clause; rules validation happens BEFORE the UPDATE specifically to avoid writing unvalidated rules the guard hot-path would then evaluate. Invalidates guard cache + publishes POLICY_UPDATED (change_type: 'updated') on success.

items.name: POST /api/policies
items.purpose: Create a new guard policy for the org.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; additionally requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin' (403 otherwise).

inputs.body.name: string, required (validated via validatePolicy)
inputs.body.agent_ids: array/string or null, optional — scopes policy to specific agents
inputs.body.created_by: string, optional — stored as-is, not derived from auth

items.response: 201 { policy: GuardPolicyRow, policy_id: string }
items.errors: 400 validation failed (details from validatePolicy); 403 non-admin; 409 duplicate name (unique constraint guard_policies_org_name_unique); 500 other.
items.gotchas: On success invalidates the guard policy cache for the org and publishes EVENTS.POLICY_UPDATED (change_type: 'created') — affects the guard hot-path immediately.

items.name: GET /api/policies/contract
items.purpose: Return the org's 'interruption contract' — a human-readable summary of what active policies will warn/block/require-approval on, derived from active policies plus 7-day fire counts.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate (read-only).
items.response: ContractView: { governed: boolean, mode_id: string|null, interrupts: Sentence[], silent: Sentence[], blocks: Sentence[], grants: [{policy_id, label, shape_key, created_at}], custom: [{policy_id, name, policy_type}], friction: {interrupts_7d, est_seconds} } where Sentence = {policy_id, text, fired_7d, editable?: {param: approval_threshold|max_spend_usd|budget_approval_threshold|budget_usd, value},…
items.errors: getDecisionCountsByPolicy failures are swallowed (.catch(() => ({}))) so the contract still renders with zero fire counts; apiErrorResponse (500) on hard failure.
items.gotchas: In demo-org context, middleware intercepts and returns demoJson(demoContract()) instead of running this handler.

items.name: POST /api/policies/generate
items.purpose: Generate guard policy drafts from natural-language input (LLM-backed), either as a dry-run preview or as created policies.
items.auth: x-api-key/session for dry_run (any org member); non-dry_run (actually creating policies) additionally requires admin role (403 otherwise).

inputs.body.answers: array of { id, value }, optional — clarification answers fed back into generatePolicies; non-array is coerced to []

items.response: dry_run=true: { drafts, assumptions, clarifications, warnings, input_hash }. dry_run=false: { created_policies: string[], count: number }.
items.errors: 400 missing/empty/oversized input_text; 403 non-admin write; 422 result.error from generatePolicies (e.g. generation failure); 500 other.
items.gotchas: Non-dry-run path loops result.drafts and calls insertPolicy per draft with a freshly minted gp_ id (16-hex slice) — no dedupe/uniqueness check against existing policy names here (unlike POST /api/policies which can 409 on unique constraint).

items.name: POST /api/policies/import
items.purpose: Import a bundled policy pack (by id) or raw YAML policy document into the org, either previewing what would be created or actually creating the policies.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; requires admin role (403 otherwise) for both preview and actual import.

inputs.body.pack: string, one of AVAILABLE_PACKS — mutually exclusive with yaml
inputs.body.yaml: string (YAML text), required if pack absent — parsed via js-yaml, expects a top-level policies array

items.response: Preview: { preview: true, would_create, would_skip, policies: [{ name, policy_type, rules, conflict, conflict_reason? }] }. Actual import: 201 { imported: number, skipped: number, errors, policies: [...] }.
items.errors: 400 neither pack nor yaml given, or invalid pack id; 404 pack file not found; unhandled errors caught by a bare try/catch returning generic 500 'Internal server error' (not apiErrorResponse) with console.error logging.
items.gotchas: Preview mode calls findPolicyByName per candidate policy to flag name conflicts (existing.length > 0) but does not create anything. Actual import delegates dedupe/creation entirely to importPolicies() in app/lib/guardrails/import-pack.ts.

items.name: GET /api/policies/loosening
items.purpose: Compute loosening proposals (candidates to relax or deactivate a policy) from the org's history of interrupt approvals, merged with any persisted human ratify/dismiss decisions.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate (read-only).

inputs.query.status: one of pending|ratified|dismissed, optional filter — 400 if invalid
inputs.query.min_fired: integer 1-100, default from LOOSENING_DEFAULTS.minFired — smoke-harness override
inputs.query.min_resolved: integer 1-100, default from LOOSENING_DEFAULTS.minResolved — smoke-harness override
inputs.query.include_synthetic: '1' to include synthetic/smoke-harness traffic in the evidence (excluded by default)

items.response: { window_days, min_fired, min_resolved, synthetic_included, inputs: { outcome_rows }, proposals: [{ ...derived fields, status, decision }], counts: { pending, ratified, dismissed } }
items.errors: 400 invalid status value; apiErrorResponse (500) on DB failure.
items.gotchas: Proposal ids (lp_...) are content-stable hashes of (rule, policy_id, action_type) — used later to validate ratify/dismiss snapshots server-side.

items.name: POST /api/policies/loosening
items.purpose: Record a human decision (ratify, dismiss, or undo) on a loosening proposal; ratify applies the actual policy relaxation (narrow the action-type envelope or deactivate the policy) in the same request.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; requires admin role (403 otherwise).

inputs.body.proposal: object snapshot { rule, policy_id, action_type? }, required for ratify/dismiss — server re-derives and integrity-checks it against proposal_id (not trusted verbatim)
inputs.body.reason: string, required for dismiss (1-500 chars, secret-redacted before storage)

items.response: undo: { ok: true, proposal_id, removed: true, change_kept: policy_id|null }. ratify/dismiss: { ok: true, proposal_id, decision, policy: updatedPolicy|null }.
items.errors: 400 invalid action/proposal_id format/snapshot mismatch/missing or oversized reason; 403 non-admin; 404 (undo) no decision recorded; 409 policy already inactive, action type no longer in envelope, or removing the last action type would empty the pol…
items.gotchas: Ratify re-validates the relaxed rules through validatePolicy before writing (same bar as PATCH /api/policies). Invalidates nothing itself but publishes EVENTS.POLICY_UPDATED on ratify; undo does NOT revert an already-applied ratify — the policy change is kept, only the decision record is deleted (audit-logged with change_kept: true).

items.name: GET /api/policies/modes
items.purpose: List the built-in Policy Modes catalog (preset governance postures) with each mode's compiled guard-policy count.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate; open to org members (no org-scoped data — reads only the static catalog).
items.response: { modes: [{ ...POLICY_MODE_CATALOG entry fields (id, human-facing posture: allows/warns/requiresApproval/blocks/toolVisibilityNotes), policy_count: number }] }
items.errors: apiErrorResponse (500) if compileMode throws unexpectedly.
items.gotchas: No org_id used at all — this is a static, org-agnostic catalog listing, not org data.

items.name: POST /api/policies/modes/import
items.purpose: Apply a named Policy Mode by compiling it to guard policies and persisting them — creating new ones or reactivating/refreshing existing ones matched by name.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; requires admin role (403 otherwise).

inputs.body.mode_id: string, required — must be a key in POLICY_MODE_CATALOG

items.response: 201 { mode_id, imported: number, reactivated: number, skipped: 0, errors: string[], policies: [{ id, name, policy_type, active }] }
items.errors: 400 missing/unknown mode_id (code: 'UNKNOWN_MODE'); per-policy compile/insert failures are caught individually and pushed into the errors array rather than failing the whole request; apiErrorResponse (500) on unexpected failure.
items.gotchas: Idempotent by design: re-applying a mode reactivates+refreshes policies previously toggled off instead of skipping them (fixes a prior bug where the cockpit got stuck showing 'No governance active'). Middleware also has a demo-mode POST intercept for this exact path (see middleware.js ~line 1466).

items.name: POST /api/policies/modes/preview
items.purpose: Compile a Policy Mode and preview its effect (generated policies, nominal decisions, and a friction simulation against recent history) without writing anything.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate — read-only, open to org members (mirrors /api/policies/generate dry_run).

inputs.body.mode_id: string, required — must be a key in POLICY_MODE_CATALOG
inputs.body.days: number > 0, optional, default 7 — friction-simulation lookback window

items.response: { mode, policies: [{ name, policy_type, decision, rules }], summary: summarizeModePack(...), friction: previewModeFriction(...) }
items.errors: 400 missing/unknown mode_id (code: 'UNKNOWN_MODE'); apiErrorResponse (500) on other failure.
items.gotchas: friction simulation is 'best-effort' per the route comment — expect an honest empty state when there's no recent history to simulate against.

items.name: GET /api/policies/proof
items.purpose: Generate a shareable 'proof' report (markdown or JSON) documenting the org's active governance policies, for external/compliance consumption.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate (read-only).
items.response: { report: string|object, format: 'md'|'json', generated_at: ISO timestamp }
items.errors: Bare try/catch returning generic 500 { error: 'Internal server error' } with console.error (not apiErrorResponse).
items.gotchas: In demo-org context, middleware intercepts this route via handleDemoPoliciesProof before the handler runs. Casts DB rows to DashClawPolicy/PolicyDoc shapes without runtime validation — relies on 'structurally compatible at runtime' comments.

items.name: GET /api/policies/proposals
items.purpose: Compute per-policy interruption stats over a rolling window plus rule-based tuning proposals (e.g. suggest deactivating dead or over-firing policies).
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate (read-only — the engine only proposes).

inputs.query.min_fired: integer 1-100, default TUNING_DEFAULTS.minFired — primarily for the smoke harness
inputs.query.include_synthetic: '1' to include smoke-harness synthetic traffic (excluded by default)

items.response: { window_days, policies: [{ policy_id, name, policy_type, active, updated_at, window_started_at, fired, approvals, override_rate, approved_risk_scores, last_fired_at }], proposals: visible[], dismissed_count, degradation }
items.errors: apiErrorResponse (500) on DB/compute failure.
items.gotchas: Proposals already dismissed (recorded via POST) are filtered out of the returned `proposals` array but counted in dismissed_count. Accepting a proposal is NOT handled by this route — the UI PATCHes the policy through /api/policies instead.

items.name: POST /api/policies/proposals
items.purpose: Dismiss or undismiss a policy-tuning proposal (does not apply the proposal itself).
items.auth: x-api-key/session; requires admin role (403 otherwise).

inputs.body.reason: string, required for dismiss (1-500 chars, trimmed, secret-redacted via redactAny before storage)

items.response: { ok: true, proposal_id, dismissed: true|false }
items.errors: 400 invalid action/proposal_id/missing or oversized reason; 403 non-admin; 404 (undismiss) proposal is not currently dismissed; apiErrorResponse (500) on other failure.
items.gotchas: Every dismiss/undismiss is written to the audit log via logActivity (action: policy_proposal.dismissed/undismissed).

items.name: GET /api/policies/review
items.purpose: Return warn-decision groups accumulated since the org's review cursor, plus recent interrupts, for the policy-review feed.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate (read-only).
items.response: { groups: groupWarnDecisions(...), interrupts: recentInterrupts[], cursor: ISO timestamp }
items.errors: apiErrorResponse (500) on DB failure.
items.gotchas: cursor defaults to (now - 7 days) if the org has no policy_review_cursor setting yet. Dismissed-shape state is read from a JSON blob setting (policy_review_dismissed) — corrupt JSON is caught and treated as 'nothing dismissed' rather than erroring. In demo-org context, middleware intercepts and returns demoJson(demoReview()).

items.name: POST /api/policies/review/verdict
items.purpose: Act on a review-feed group with one of six verdicts: mark as fine (dismiss the shape), always-allow (create an allow_grant policy), tighten (create require_approval or protected_path policy), mark the whole feed reviewed (advance the cursor), or a retrospective Yes/No on the group (retro_fine / retro_stop) that feeds the calibration controller as a warn_review-sourced adjudication (weight 0.5, never moves θ in the tightening direction).
items.auth: x-api-key/session; requires admin role (403 otherwise).

inputs.body.shape: { action_type: string (required for all verdicts except mark_all_reviewed, max 128 chars), target_prefix?: string|null (max 256 chars) }

items.response: mark_all_reviewed: { ok: true, cursor }. fine: { ok: true, dismissed: key }. always_allow/tighten: 201 { ok: true, policy }.
items.errors: 400 invalid verdict, missing shape.action_type, or oversized action_type/target_prefix; 403 non-admin; 409 a rule for this shape already exists (unique constraint); apiErrorResponse (500) other.
items.gotchas: This route inserts policies directly via insertPolicy, bypassing validatePolicy — so it hand-enforces the same length caps (action_type ≤128, target_prefix ≤256) as validate.js to avoid guard hot-path bloat. 'tighten' produces protected_path when target_prefix looks like a path (contains '/'), else require_approval scoped to the shape's target_prefix (never org-wide) — narrowing this scope was a …

items.name: POST /api/policies/simulate
items.purpose: Dry-run a candidate policy (not yet saved) against the org's recent historical actions to preview what decisions it would have produced.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate (this route only reads history and evaluates in-memory; it writes nothing).
items.response: { summary: { total, matches, block, warn, require_approval, allow }, matches: [{ action_id, goal, agent_name, timestamp, original_status, simulated_action, simulated_reason }], sample_size, window_days } — or, when no historical actions exist: { summary: {...zeros}, matches: [], message: '...' }
items.errors: 400 missing policy_type or rules; bare try/catch returning generic 500 { error: 'Internal server error' } with console.error (not apiErrorResponse).
items.gotchas: Uses the same evaluatePolicy() function as the real guard hot-path (app/lib/guard.ts), with a dummyPolicy id 'sim_1', so simulation results should match real enforcement behavior for that rule set. Middleware has a demo-mode POST intercept for this path.

items.name: GET /api/policies/summary
items.purpose: Read-only posture summary for the /policies cockpit page: current mode(s), enforcement rule buckets, compiled rule list, shield states, 30-day decision outcomes, agent count, and pending-approval count.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate (read-only).
items.response: PolicySummary: { governed: boolean, modes: [{id, name, interruptionLevel}], primaryMode: mode|null, enforcement: {total, warn, require_approval, block}, rules: [{id, name, bucket: allow|warn|require_approval|block, fired30d, lastFiredAt}], shields: [{id, name, description, on, fired30d, lastFiredAt}], decisions30d: {total, allow, warn, require_approval, block}, scope: {allAgents: boolean}, agents…
items.errors: apiErrorResponse (500) only for the un-caught getActivePolicies call; the other four queries (agents, fire counts, outcome counts, action stats) are each individually .catch()'d to zero/empty defaults so a failing analytics query degrades gracefully…
items.gotchas: pendingApprovals is derived from getActionStats().current.approval, defaulting to 0 if absent/NaN.

items.name: GET /api/policies/templates
items.purpose: List the available policy-pack templates (bundled YAML packs) with their metadata and the policies each pack contains, for the import/onboarding UI.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate; open to org members — reads only static pack files on disk, not org data.
items.response: { templates: [{ id, name, description, recommended_for, policy_count, policies: [{ name, policy_type, rules_summary }] }] }
items.errors: Bare try/catch returning generic 500 { error: 'Failed to load templates' } (not apiErrorResponse); a pack with unreadable/missing YAML is skipped individually with a console.warn rather than failing the whole list.
items.gotchas: Reads pack files directly from disk at app/lib/guardrails/packs/<packId>/policies.yml via process.cwd() — depends on the deployed filesystem layout, not the database.

items.name: POST /api/policies/test
items.purpose: Run test recipes against a policy's rules through the real enforcement evaluator (recipe mode, for a not-yet-saved policy), or re-run the derived tests of all currently active org policies (legacy mode).
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate.

inputs.body.policy_type: string — presence of policy_type + rules together selects recipe mode; absence falls back to legacy mode (no body required)
inputs.body.rules: string (JSON) or object — required for recipe mode
inputs.body.tests: array of { name?, input, expect: { decision } }, optional — recipe list; if absent, falls back to rules.tests

items.response: Recipe mode: { results: { total_policies: 1, total_tests, passed, failed, success, details: [{ policy_id: 'recipe', policy_name, tests: [{ name, passed, expected, actual, reason }] }] }, mode: 'recipe', generated_at }. Legacy mode: { results: { total_policies, total_tests, passed, failed, success, details: [{ policy_id, policy_name, tests }] }, generated_at } (no `mode` field).
items.errors: 400 rules is not valid JSON / not an object (recipe mode only); bare try/catch returning generic 500 { error: 'Internal server error' } with console.error (not apiErrorResponse).
items.gotchas: Recipe mode uses the real guard evaluatePolicy() (same as /simulate) so results reflect actual enforcement; legacy mode instead uses evaluateGuardrailPolicy() from the separate guardrails converter/evaluator path and, unlike recipe mode, persists the run via createTestRun (gtr_ id) — recipe-mode runs are NOT persisted. Middleware has a demo-mode POST intercept for this path.

items.name: GET /api/policies/tightening
items.purpose: Compute tightening proposals (candidates to newly govern an ungoverned but risky action pattern) from the org's ungoverned-allow decision history, merged with persisted human ratify/dismiss decisions.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; no admin gate (read-only).

inputs.query.status: one of pending|ratified|dismissed, optional filter — 400 if invalid
inputs.query.include_synthetic: '1' to include synthetic/smoke traffic (excluded by default)

items.response: { window_days, min_observed, synthetic_included, inputs: { decisions }, proposals: [{ ...derived, status, decision }], counts: { pending, ratified, dismissed } }
items.errors: 400 invalid status; apiErrorResponse (500) on DB/compute failure.
items.gotchas: Grouped by (action_type × risk_level) the same way v3.1's review_incident posture findings are, so a tightening proposal and a posture finding mirror each other 1:1 via finding_key. Proposal ids (tp_...) are content-stable hashes of (action_type, risk_level).

items.name: POST /api/policies/tightening
items.purpose: Record a human decision (ratify, dismiss, or undo) on a tightening proposal; ratify creates the actual require_approval policy and resolves the mirrored posture finding in the same request.
items.auth: x-api-key/session; requires admin role (403 otherwise).

inputs.body.proposal: object snapshot { rule, action_type, risk_level: 'high'|'critical' }, required for ratify/dismiss — server re-derives and integrity-checks against proposal_id
inputs.body.reason: string, required for dismiss (1-500 chars, secret-redacted via redactAny)

items.response: undo: { ok: true, proposal_id, removed: true, policy_kept: policy_id|null }. ratify/dismiss: { ok: true, proposal_id, decision, policy: newPolicy|null }.
items.errors: 400 invalid action/proposal_id/snapshot mismatch/missing or oversized reason; 403 non-admin; 404 (undo) no decision recorded; 409 a policy named `[Tightened] <action_type>` already exists; apiErrorResponse (500) other.
items.gotchas: Ratify creates a require_approval policy (name `[Tightened] <action_type>`, truncated to 200 chars) via insertPolicy bypassing validatePolicy, publishes EVENTS.POLICY_UPDATED, and marks the mirrored posture finding 'resolved' via setFindingState. Undo deletes only the decision record — a policy already created by a prior ratify is deliberately kept (audit-logged with policy_kept).

items.name: GET /api/prompts/agent-connect/raw
items.purpose: Serve the static dashclaw-agent-connect.md markdown file (docs/prompts/) for the public 'Copy Agent-Connect Prompt' button.
items.auth: public — explicitly listed in middleware.js PUBLIC_ROUTES ('/api/prompts/agent-connect/raw')
items.response: 200 text/markdown body of docs/prompts/dashclaw-agent-connect.md
items.errors: 404 JSON { error: 'Prompt not found' } if the file can't be read
items.gotchas: Reads directly from the filesystem (readFileSync) at request time, not from the DB — content updates only via a code/docs deploy; note the bare '/api/prompts' prefix is explicitly NOT public (a prior version leaked the whole prompts API) — only this and two sibling /raw routes are allowlisted.

items.name: GET /api/prompts/sdk-coverage/raw
items.purpose: Serves the raw markdown file docs/prompts/dashclaw-sdk-coverage.md for a 'Copy Prompt' button.
items.auth: public — explicitly listed in middleware.js PUBLIC_ROUTES (unauthenticated static markdown)
items.response: raw text/markdown body (Content-Type: text/markdown; charset=utf-8), not JSON
items.errors: 404 { error: 'Prompt not found' } if the file is missing/unreadable
items.gotchas: Reads from disk via fs.readFileSync at request time (force-dynamic); no DB, no org scoping.

items.name: GET /api/prompts/server-setup/raw
items.purpose: Serves the raw markdown file docs/prompts/dashclaw-server-setup.md for a 'Copy Prompt' button.
items.auth: public — explicitly listed in middleware.js PUBLIC_ROUTES and in DEMO_PASSTHROUGH_EXACT (works identically in demo mode)
items.response: raw text/markdown body, not JSON
items.errors: 404 { error: 'Prompt not found' } if the file is missing/unreadable
items.gotchas: Same static-file pattern as sdk-coverage/raw.

items.name: GET /api/signals
items.purpose: Computes and returns current risk signals for the org (optionally filtered to one agent) via app/lib/signals computeSignals. Occurrences dismissed via POST /api/signals are subtracted server-side before the response.
items.auth: x-api-key
items.response: { signals: Signal[], counts: { red, amber, total }, lastUpdated } Also returns `muted`: the signals currently hidden by a dismissal ({ type, label, agent_id, mcp_server, severity, dismiss_key }), which backs the panel’s Restore control.
items.errors: 500 { error: 'An error occurred while computing risk signals', signals: [], counts: { red:0, amber:0, total:0 } } — error body still includes empty signals/counts so callers don't need special-case handling
items.gotchas: Per project memory (reference_dashclaw_signals_rewrite_and_reputation_scale), signals severity here is red/amber (not numeric); the module caches its own sql client at module scope (getSql helper) separate from the shared db.ts default export pattern used elsewhere.

items.name: POST /api/signals
items.purpose: Dismisses signals server-side (signal_dismissals table) so every surface — status bar, decisions signals panel, widget pulse, guard warnings, signals cron — subtracts the same set. For event-time signal types the key is a per-occurrence signalDismissKey and a new occurrence re-fires. For SAMPLED-time types (autonomy_spike, repeated_failures, assumption_drift, session_stalled, mcp_degraded) the key omits the timestamp and the dismissal is a durable mute — on (type, agent) for most, and on (type, server) for mcp_degraded, whose per-server signals carry whichever agent_id happened to observe them — reversed with DELETE.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware; requires x-org-role === 'admin' (muting hides a live risk condition from the whole org)

inputs.body.dismiss_keys: string[], required, 1-1000 keys, each <= 600 chars, each the six-slot colon-joined form signalDismissKey mints (leading with a known signal type)

items.response: { dismissed: number, received: number } — dismissed counts only newly-inserted keys; re-dismissing is an idempotent no-op
items.errors: 400 on a missing/empty/oversized dismiss_keys array, non-string keys, or keys failing the shape gate; 403 Admin access required for non-admin roles; 500 { error } on a write failure
items.gotchas: Dismissal is a human triage action surfaced in the /decisions Governance Signals panel — it is deliberately not an SDK method. Sampled-time types mute durably because their detected_at is a sampling time that advances on its own; including it made those signals impossible to clear. Browsers holding the legacy localStorage dismissed set (dashclaw_dismissed_signals) bulk-migrate it here once via the SystemStatusBar, then delete the local copy.

items.name: DELETE /api/signals
items.purpose: Restores (un-mutes) previously dismissed signals by removing their rows from signal_dismissals. Ships alongside the durable mute: sampled-time signal types mute on (type, agent) rather than per occurrence, so without a restore path one click could hide a live condition permanently.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved to org via middleware; requires x-org-role === 'admin' (same gate as POST)

inputs.body.dismiss_keys: string[], required, 1-1000 keys, each <= 600 chars (same caps and six-slot shape gate as POST)

items.response: { restored: number, received: number } — restored counts only rows actually deleted; restoring a key that was never dismissed is an idempotent no-op
items.errors: 400 on a missing/empty/oversized dismiss_keys array, non-string keys, or keys failing the shape gate; 403 Admin access required for non-admin roles; 500 { error } on a delete failure
items.gotchas: The keys to pass come from the `muted` array on GET /api/signals, not from the live signals list. The /decisions Governance Signals panel exposes this as the "Muted N" chip with per-entry and bulk Restore buttons.

items.name: GET /api/security/prompt-injection
items.purpose: Lists previously stored prompt-injection scan records for the org, paginated.
items.auth: Not in PUBLIC_ROUTES — standard middleware x-api-key/session auth; getOrgId(request) reads the trusted x-org-id header middleware forwards. No admin-role check.
items.response: { scans: array, total: number }
items.errors: 500 { error: 'An error occurred fetching prompt injection scans' }
items.gotchas: listScans/insertScan come from app/lib/repositories/promptInjection.repository — not independently re-verified for exact column shape in this pass.

items.name: POST /api/security/prompt-injection
items.purpose: Scans a text payload for prompt-injection patterns (via lib/promptInjection.scanForPromptInjection) and optionally persists scan metadata (never the raw content) for audit/history.
items.auth: Not in PUBLIC_ROUTES — standard middleware x-api-key/session auth.

inputs.body.store: boolean, optional — defaults to storing (store !== false) when findings_count > 0

items.response: { clean: boolean, risk_level: string, recommendation: string, findings_count: number, critical_count: number, categories: array, findings: array, source: string|null }
items.errors: 400 { error: 'text is required' } if missing; 400 { error: 'text must be a string' } if wrong type; 500 { error: 'An error occurred during prompt injection scan' }
items.gotchas: Only content_hash (sha256 of raw text) is stored, never the raw text itself — by design, per inline comment. Storage failure is swallowed with a console.error (doesn't fail the request/response). store defaults to true implicitly (only store === false skips persistence), and only persists when findings_count > 0 regardless of store flag.

items.name: GET /api/security/status
items.purpose: Computes a security health score (0-100) for the org: checks ENCRYPTION_KEY presence/length, DATABASE_URL presence, count of unencrypted sensitive settings, and whether a webhook SSRF allowlist (WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_DOMAINS) is configured.
items.auth: Not in PUBLIC_ROUTES; standard middleware auth PLUS an explicit admin-only gate in the handler: getOrgRole(request) !== 'admin' returns 403.
items.response: { score: number (0-100), checks: [{ id, status: 'ok'|'warning'|'critical'|'info', label, detail? }], timestamp: ISO string }
items.errors: 403 { error: 'Forbidden - admin role required', score: 0, checks: [], timestamp } if role isn't admin; 500 { error: 'Failed to generate security report', score: 0, checks: [], timestamp } on failure
items.gotchas: Score deductions: -40 missing encryption key, -10 wrong-length key (must be exactly 32 chars for AES-256), -40 missing DATABASE_URL, -5 per unencrypted sensitive setting found, floored at 0. Unencrypted-settings check excludes an explicit allowlist of known-non-sensitive keys despite matching a sensitive-looking LIKE pattern (e.g. TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID). Demo mode has a fixture rout…

items.name: GET /api/self-governance
items.purpose: Public aggregate proof that this instance governs real work (the /proof surface) — counts of action_records and guard_decisions, excluding synthetic/test traffic.
items.auth: public — but only when the operator has opted in via DASHCLAW_SELF_GOVERNANCE_PUBLIC=true; otherwise 404. Middleware explicitly allows this exact path+GET without an API key (isSelfGovernancePublicRe…
items.response: { selfGovernance: true, version, generatedAt, ...stats } where stats includes action/decision totals, last30d/last7d counts, first_at/latest_at, active_days (from getSelfGovernanceStats)
items.errors: 404 { error: 'Not found' } when DASHCLAW_SELF_GOVERNANCE_PUBLIC != 'true' — this is the default off state on every instance except the one governing this repo's own maintenance
items.gotchas: 60-second in-memory response cache (module-level, per server instance) to protect the DB from an unauthenticated hot loop. Confirms project memory: this route IS the public /proof surface, aggregate-only, no org identifiers, gated by an explicit env flag rather than auth.

items.name: GET /api/session/effective
items.purpose: Returns the caller's own effective viewer role, unifying NextAuth-JWT and local-password session cookies (fixes admins on the local-auth path being misread as members by useSession()).
items.auth: public — explicitly in middleware.js PUBLIC_ROUTES; reads only the requester's own cookie, never org data
items.response: { authenticated: boolean, authType: string|null, role: string|null, isAdmin: boolean }
items.errors: none beyond default framework errors; always 200 with authenticated:false for anonymous callers
items.gotchas: Deliberately public so unauthenticated pages (marketing, /login) can gate client fetches without a console 401 for every visitor — it never returns org-scoped data, only the caller's own session state.

items.name: DELETE /api/settings
items.purpose: Remove an org-level or agent-specific setting.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin'.

inputs.query.agent_id: string, optional — deletes agent-specific row only; omitted deletes org-level row (agent_id IS NULL)

items.response: { success: true, deleted: key, agent_id: agentId || null }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 400 if key missing (error message includes 'required'); 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: Logs an audit activity entry ('setting.deleted'). Deleting without agent_id only removes the org-default row, not any per-agent overrides.

items.name: GET /api/settings
items.purpose: Fetch org (and optionally per-agent) settings, with sensitive values masked or decrypted depending on caller privilege.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie. No explicit admin gate — any authenticated caller can read, but decryption/masking depends on role and auth method.

inputs.query.agent_id: string, optional — merges agent overrides with org defaults

items.response: { settings: [{ ...row, value, hasValue: boolean }] } — value is the decrypted plaintext only when caller used an x-api-key AND role==='admin'; otherwise masked (maskValue) for encrypted/sensitive keys or for any non-admin role.
items.errors: 500 on any error (ensureSettingsTable or fetch failure).
items.gotchas: Decryption ('canDecrypt') requires BOTH: request authenticated via x-api-key header (not a browser session) AND role==='admin'. Browser sessions (even admin) always see masked secret values. Members never see unmasked values for anything, sensitive or not.

items.name: POST /api/settings
