items.purpose: Create or update an org- or agent-level setting, auto-encrypting sensitive keys.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin'.

inputs.body.key: string, required (validated against VALID_SETTING_KEYS in repository)

items.response: { success: true, key, agent_id } or { success: true, key, agent_id, skipped: true } if the submitted value was a masked placeholder.
items.errors: 503 in production if ENCRYPTION_KEY env var is missing; 403 if not admin; 400 if key/category invalid (message includes 'Invalid'/'required'); 500 on encryption failure or other errors.
items.gotchas: If value contains the literal masked-placeholder string '••••••••' (i.e. the UI echoed back a masked value unedited), the write is silently skipped (skipped:true) rather than overwriting the real secret with the mask. shouldAutoEncrypt() forces encryption for keys it deems sensitive regardless of the 'encrypted' flag passed in. Logs an audit activity entry ('setting.updated').

items.name: POST /api/settings/test
items.purpose: Test a third-party integration's credentials (Neon, Supabase, Notion, GitHub, OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Together, Replicate, Brave, ElevenLabs, Discord, Slack, Linear, Resend, Stripe, Cloudflare, Vercel, or a generic fallback) by making a live call with the provided credentials.
items.auth: Checks request.headers.get('x-org-role') === 'admin' directly (not via getOrgRole helper, but middleware sets the same header) — admin only.

inputs.body.integration: string, required — one of the supported provider keys or any other string (falls through to generic test)
inputs.body.credentials: object, required — provider-specific fields e.g. DATABASE_URL, NOTION_API_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, etc.

items.response: { success: boolean, message: string } — provider-specific success/failure message (e.g. 'Connected as @user', 'Database connection successful!').
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 500 with { success:false, message:'Connection test failed' } on unexpected exceptions; individual provider tests return 200 with success:false for invalid credentials rather than error statuses.
items.gotchas: SSRF-hardened: all outbound fetches for URL-bearing integrations (Neon DATABASE_URL, Supabase URL, Discord webhook) are validated against allowlist regexes and isPrivateIP() before the request is sent, and go through the shared safeFetch (app/lib/url-safety.js) with HTTPS enforcement and manual-redirect handling. Discord additionally requires the target host to be discord.com with an /api/webhook…

items.name: POST /api/setup/live-proof
items.purpose: Mints a live-verification proof token from a client-submitted verification payload (e.g. from a CI/local verification run) and returns a shareable /setup?proof=... URL plus a downloadable proof URL.
items.auth: NOT in middleware.js PUBLIC_ROUTES (only /api/setup/status, /api/setup/proof, /api/setup/ping, /api/setup/migrate are listed there) — so this route goes through normal middleware x-api-key/session au…

inputs.body.tool: string, optional, normalized tool id of the validator run
inputs.body.host: string, optional, overridden by the request host when present (120-char cap)
inputs.body.summary: {passed, failed, skipped, score(0-100)} — REQUIRED in effect: the request is rejected unless failed === 0 AND passed > 0
inputs.body.checks: array, optional, summarized into the proof

items.response: { ok: true, proof, proof_token: string, setup_url: string, proof_download_url: string }
items.errors: 400 { error: message } on any thrown error (invalid payload or missing signing secret, per createLiveVerificationProofToken)
items.gotchas: Body is normalized by app/lib/liveVerificationProof.mjs: only successful runs mint a proof (throws 'Only successful live validation runs can be captured as proof.' -> 400 when summary.failed > 0 or summary.passed === 0). proof_token is an HS256 JWT signed with NEXTAUTH_SECRET, 7-day expiry. Not in PUBLIC_ROUTES, so it needs a valid x-api-key despite living under /api/setup/.

items.name: POST /api/setup/migrate
items.purpose: Runtime database migration safety net: applies all Drizzle SQL migrations (or an inline critical-tables DDL fallback), reconciles action_records runtime columns/indexes, seeds org_default, and optionally seeds an admin API key from DASHCLAW_API_KEY. Idempotent.
items.auth: Public route in middleware.js (bypasses x-api-key entirely). Self-guards: if the instance is already initialized (org_default + core tables exist per isAlreadyInitialized), requires an admin-scoped A…
items.response: { ok: true, schema: { applied: number, skipped: number }, org_seeded: boolean, key_seeded: boolean }
items.errors: 500 { error: 'DATABASE_URL is not set...' } if no DATABASE_URL; 401 { error: 'Instance already initialized. Admin API key required...' } if already initialized and caller isn't an authorized admin; 500 { error: redactErrorDetail(err) } on any other …
items.gotchas: Public + no-auth ONLY during first-run bootstrap — after org_default exists, an admin API key is mandatory, preventing an unauthenticated caller from re-seeding plan='pro' or wiping state. DDL is read from the drizzle/ directory at runtime (readdirSync + readFileSync), falling back to the CRITICAL_TABLES_DDL constant in this same file if that directory isn't in the serverless bundle — that fallba…

items.name: POST /api/setup/ping
items.purpose: Authenticated liveness check used by the setup UI to confirm the instance accepts real API-key requests; on success also mints a live-verification proof token so the setup page can upgrade to a 'verified' state.
items.auth: Public route in middleware.js (bypasses standard middleware auth) but self-guards inside the handler: reads x-api-key header, checks it against DASHCLAW_API_KEY env (timingSafeCompare fast path) or a…
items.response: { ok: true, latencyMs: number, message: string, proof_token: string|null }
items.errors: 403 { ok: false, message: 'Live ping is not available in demo mode.' } when DASHCLAW_MODE=demo; 401 { ok: false, message: 'API key did not match.' } when x-api-key missing or invalid
items.gotchas: proof_token minting is best-effort (needs NEXTAUTH_SECRET) — null if it fails, request still succeeds. DB lookup failure on the slow path silently falls through to the final 401 rather than 500ing.

items.name: GET /api/setup/proof
items.purpose: Returns (or downloads) the current readiness/verification proof artifact for this instance, optionally upgraded by a live-verification proof token passed in the query string, and adjusted for whether the caller is authenticated (via session cookie).
items.auth: Public route in middleware.js — no API key required. Reads the session cookie header directly to derive isAuthenticated via getViewerContextFromCookieHeader, which affects what projectReadinessReport…

inputs.query.proof: optional live-verification proof token string, read via readLiveVerificationProofToken

items.response: Proof artifact: { artifact_version: 1, generated_at, checked_at, route: '/setup', viewer_mode: 'operator'|'public', host, verification: {overall, label, summary, ready, fully_verified, readiness_status}, runtime: {node_version, node_env}, categories: [{id, title, status, summary, what_was_checked, evidence_summary, pending_proof, checks: [{id, label, status, detail, sub_detail, likely_cause, next…
items.errors: 500 { error: 'Internal server error' } on any thrown exception
items.gotchas: Content is always 'Cache-Control: no-store'. download=1 triggers a filename dashclaw-setup-proof-<timestamp>.json attachment. Exact projected fields depend on app/lib/readiness.mjs, not re-derived here — treat the proof artifact's internal shape as defined there.

items.name: GET /api/setup/status
items.purpose: Thin wrapper reporting whether the dashboard/instance is configured (DB reachable, schema initialized, etc.) for the setup UI's readiness check.
items.auth: Public route in middleware.js — no auth at all, by design (needed before an operator has any API key).
items.response: Configured: { configured: true, message: 'Dashboard is configured' }. Not configured: { configured: false, reason: 'missing_database_url'|'no_tables'|'connection_error', message, missing_tables?: number, missing?: string[] (core table names, only for no_tables) }
items.errors: On thrown error, falls back to 200 (not an error status) with { configured: false, reason: 'connection_error', message: 'Unable to connect to database' } — note this handler always returns HTTP 200, encoding failure in the body rather than the statu…
items.gotchas: Always returns HTTP 200, encoding failure in the body (configured: false) rather than the status code — callers must check the configured field, not response.ok.

items.name: GET /api/stream
items.purpose: Server-Sent Events feed of org events (actions, messages, policy updates, decisions, loops, goals, signals, token usage) with replay-from-cursor support.
items.auth: x-api-key (standard middleware auth); demo mode is forwarded through with a synthetic org_demo/admin header pair rather than blocked

inputs.query.lastEventId: optional cursor, also accepted via Last-Event-ID header

items.response: text/event-stream; named SSE events (action_created, message_created, policy_updated, decision_created, guard_decision_created, loop_created/updated, goal_created/updated, signal_detected, token_usage) each with a payload + cursor id; an initial 'connected' event reports replay stats
items.errors: 503 'Realtime backend unavailable' if realtime health check fails; 500 'Internal Server Error' on unexpected throw
items.gotchas: 15s heartbeat comments keep proxies from killing the connection; hard 30-minute max connection duration (auto-closes); dedupes by cursor with a 10k-entry seen-set that clears when full; replay runs after the Response is returned (avoids backpressure deadlock) and live events are buffered until replay completes.

items.name: GET /api/team-tasks
items.purpose: List team tasks for the org (the multi-agent /team task timeline), optionally filtered by status, newest first.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.
items.response: 200: { tasks: [...team_tasks rows] } ordered by created_at DESC.
items.errors: 500 Failed to list team tasks
items.gotchas: The status filter is not validated against TEAM_TASK_STATUSES at this route (only POST/PATCH validate it) — an unrecognized status value just returns zero rows silently instead of a 400.

items.name: POST /api/team-tasks
items.purpose: Create a new team task — the root of a multi-agent /team task timeline (THESIS.md "fleets and teams" amendment) — with a client-minted id.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.

inputs.body.lead_agent: string, required, any lowercase agent-id slug matching TEAM_AGENT_ID_PATTERN (e.g. claude|openclaw|moltfire)
inputs.body.status: string, optional, one of TEAM_TASK_STATUSES, defaults to 'open'

items.response: 201: { task }
items.errors: 400 id/instruction required, invalid origin/lead_agent/status; 409 task already exists (duplicate id); 500 Failed to create team task
items.gotchas: Task ids are minted client-side (by the clawd team-ledger), not server-generated — a duplicate id 409s rather than silently overwriting. Publishes team_task.created on the org SSE stream after insert (fire-and-forget, not awaited).

items.name: GET /api/team-tasks/{taskId}
items.purpose: Fetch one team task plus its full event timeline in a single call.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.
items.response: 200: { task, events: [...team_task_events rows, ordered ts ASC] }
items.errors: 404 task not found; 500 Failed to get team task
items.gotchas: The embedded events list uses listTeamTaskEvents's default limit (500), not a client-supplied one — unlike the dedicated GET .../events route, this endpoint takes no limit param.

items.name: PATCH /api/team-tasks/{taskId}
items.purpose: Update a team task's status or session-binding fields (claude_session_id / openclaw_session_key).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.
items.response: 200: { task }
items.errors: 400 invalid status / nothing to update (status, claude_session_id, and openclaw_session_key all omitted); 404 task not found; 500 Failed to update team task
items.gotchas: At least one of status/claude_session_id/openclaw_session_key must be present or the route 400s before touching the DB; updated_at is bumped to now() on every successful update regardless of which fields changed.

items.name: GET /api/team-tasks/{taskId}/events
items.purpose: List the event timeline for one team task (delegations, replies, status changes, results).
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.
items.response: 200: { events: [...] } ordered ts ASC.
items.errors: 500 Failed to list team task events
items.gotchas: No 404 for an unknown taskId — it just returns { events: [] }, unlike GET /api/team-tasks/{taskId} which 404s on a missing task.

items.name: POST /api/team-tasks/{taskId}/events
items.purpose: Append one event to a team task's timeline (delegation, reply, status change, approval-needed, result, error, done) — the write side of the multi-agent handoff protocol.
items.auth: x-api-key resolved by middleware to org_id/role (or session cookie); no admin-role gate.

inputs.body.ts: ISO timestamp, optional, defaults to now()
inputs.body.from_agent: string, required, any lowercase agent-id slug matching TEAM_AGENT_ID_PATTERN (e.g. claude|openclaw|moltfire|mission-control)
inputs.body.to_agent: string, required, any lowercase agent-id slug matching TEAM_AGENT_ID_PATTERN (e.g. claude|openclaw|wes|forge)
inputs.body.action_id: string, optional — links the event to a governed action

items.response: 201: { event }
items.errors: 400 invalid from_agent/to_agent/type, summary required; 404 task not found (guarded INSERT returns no row rather than a foreign-key violation); 500 Failed to append team task event
items.gotchas: The INSERT is guarded with a WHERE EXISTS against team_tasks instead of relying on a DB foreign-key violation, so a bad taskId cleanly 404s rather than 500ing. Publishes team_task.event on the org SSE stream after insert (fire-and-forget).

items.name: POST /api/telegram/webhook
items.purpose: Telegram bot webhook handling inline-keyboard approve/deny callback presses on pending-approval action notifications.
items.auth: NOT x-api-key — verifies x-telegram-bot-api-secret-token header (timing-safe compare against TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET) plus a sender chat_id allowlist against TELEGRAM_ADMIN_CHAT_ID; public route (lis…

inputs.body: Telegram Update JSON; only callback_query is handled, callback_query.data must match /^(ap|dn):(act_[a-z0-9_-]{1,57})$/

items.response: { ok: true } for all handled/ignored cases (Telegram doesn't need the outcome — feedback goes back via editMessageText on the original message)
items.errors: 401 Unauthorized (bad secret token or sender not the allowlisted admin chat, same status for both to avoid revealing which check failed); 400 Invalid JSON
items.gotchas: TELEGRAM_APPROVER_ORG_ID must be set or it edits the Telegram message with a misconfiguration warning and returns ok; callback is ack'd immediately (answerCallbackQuery) before DB work so Telegram doesn't retry on slow queries; chat_id used for edits is always the trusted admin env var, never the body-provided one; recordApproval returning null (already resolved by another channel) is handled dis…

items.name: DELETE /api/webhooks
items.purpose: Delete a webhook by id.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires admin role.
items.response: { success: true, deleted: webhookId }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 400 if id missing/malformed; 404 if webhook not found for this org; 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: Logs 'webhook.deleted' audit activity. Lookup/delete is scoped to (webhookId, orgId) so cross-tenant deletion isn't possible even with a guessed id.

items.name: GET /api/webhooks
items.purpose: List all webhooks configured for the org, with secrets masked.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie. No role gate — any org member can list webhooks (secrets are masked for everyone).
items.response: { webhooks: [{...row, secret: '••••••••••••••••••••••••••••XXXX' (partially masked, last 2 chars always hidden) or null}] }
items.errors: 500 on unexpected error.
items.gotchas: Secret masking reveals 4 characters (positions -6 to -2 from the end) while always hiding the final 2 characters, so the full secret is never fully reconstructable from this response even in fragments.

items.name: POST /api/webhooks
items.purpose: Register a new webhook destination for the org.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie; requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin'.

inputs.body.events: string[], optional, default ['all']; each must be one of the VALID_EVENT_TYPES list (all, autonomy_spike, high_impact_low_oversight, repeated_failures, stale_loop, assumption_drift, stale_assumption,…

items.response: 201 { webhook: { id, url, secret (raw, shown once), events, active: 1, created_at }, storageWarning: string }
items.errors: 403 if not admin; 400 if URL invalid (message from isValidWebhookUrl) or events empty/not-an-array/contains an invalid type; 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: The signing secret (32 random bytes hex) is returned in full only on this create call — GET /api/webhooks masks it afterward. Logs 'webhook.created' audit activity with url+events.

items.name: GET /api/webhooks/{webhookId}/deliveries
items.purpose: List recent delivery attempts (with status/response info) for a specific webhook.
items.auth: x-api-key (resolved by middleware to org_id/role) or session cookie. No role gate — any org member can view delivery history.
items.response: { deliveries: [...] } — includes payload and response_body fields, which are redacted at write time (not at read time) per an inline code comment referencing redactForStorage in app/lib/webhooks.ts.
items.errors: 400 if webhookId malformed; 404 if webhook not found for this org; 500 otherwise.
items.gotchas: payload/response_body are safe to expose here because sensitive data was already redacted when the delivery was logged (logWebhookDelivery), not filtered at read time — so if redaction logic there ever regresses, this endpoint would expose it.

items.name: POST /api/webhooks/{webhookId}/test
items.purpose: Send a synthetic test payload to a webhook's configured URL to verify it's receiving events, using the real HMAC delivery pipeline (deliverWebhook).

items.response: { success: boolean, response_status: number }

Logs 'webhook.tested' audit activity with success/status.

items.name: GET /api/widget/pulse
items.purpose: The snapshot behind the /widget Pulse surface (v5.15, DashClaw Pulse): one composed, whitelisted payload — pending approvals (count + up to 5 rows ordered for dwell), red/amber signal counts, agent activity, last-action recency, and a machine-local desktop-presence verdict. Design + honesty rules: docs/decisions/2026-08-09-widget-pulse.md.
items.auth: Authenticated org context (API key or signed-in session; middleware injects x-org-id). 401 without it.

items.auth: x-api-key (standard middleware auth) PLUS in-route admin gate: requires getOrgRole(request) === 'admin'

package.name: dashclaw
package.description: Minimal governance runtime for AI agents. Intercept, govern, and verify agent actions.
package.moduleSystem: ESM-first (type: module). ESM entry: dashclaw.js; CJS entry: index.cjs (a lazy async bridge that dynamically imports the ESM module; error classes use a Symbol.hasInstance placeholder pattern so instanceof works across the ESM/CJS boundary). Zero runtime dependencies.

..note: Canonical client. Named exports: DashClaw, ApprovalDeniedError, GuardBlockedError, scrubAct.

bin.note: npx dashclaw <args> is a pure forwarding shim: spawns npm exec --yes -- @dashclaw/cli <args>. The SDK package owns the bare npm name but the real CLI lives in @dashclaw/cli. Not a programmatic API surface.

constructor.signature: new DashClaw({ baseUrl, apiKey, agentId, agentName?, authToken? })

baseUrl.meaning: DashClaw instance base URL (trailing slash stripped). Constructor throws "baseUrl is required" if missing.

apiKey.meaning: API key sent as x-api-key header on every request. Constructor throws if missing.

agentId.meaning: Unique identifier for this agent; auto-injected into guard/createAction/messages/etc. Constructor throws if missing.

agentName.meaning: Human-readable label stored in the audit trail for attribution.

authToken.meaning: Phase 2 cryptographic attribution: a JWT from your OIDC provider, sent as Authorization: Bearer. Server verifies via JWKS; the JWT sub claim overrides agentId in the audit record when verification succeeds. Guard responses then carry verification_status (verified|unverified|expired|failed|unknown_issuer).

constructor.envConvention: The SDK itself reads NO env vars — you wire them yourself. Conventional names used across README/docs/CLI: DASHCLAW_BASE_URL (or DASHCLAW_URL in MCP contexts), DASHCLAW_API_KEY, optional DASHCLAW_AGENT_ID. The @dashclaw/cli resolves env vars -> ~/.dashclaw/config.json -> interactive prompt.
constructor.namespaces: constructor also builds claw.execution.capabilities.{list,create,get,update,invoke,test,getHealth,listHealth,getHistory} — thin arrows onto the flat listCapabilities/createCapability/... methods. The namespaced paths are the canonical target for new capability work.

errorHandling.model: All HTTP calls go through a single _request helper. Non-OK responses throw. Two custom error classes are exported; everything else surfaces as a plain Error with extra fields.
errorHandling.GuardBlockedError: Thrown by ANY SDK call when the server returns HTTP 403 with { decision: { decision: "block" } } — the request-level policy block. NOTE: a guard() call that returns { decision: "block" } in a 200 body does NOT throw; check decision.decision yourself and throw new GuardBlockedError(decision) to abort. Also thrown by runGoverned()/guardedFetch() when guard returns block. Fields: .name, .message (decision.reason), .decision.
errorHandling.ApprovalDeniedError: Thrown by waitForApproval() (and runGoverned/guardedFetch when they wait) when an operator denies the action (status becomes failed or cancelled) or the approval expires server-side (status expired — check err.status to distinguish). Fields: .name, .message, .decision (the action).
errorHandling.genericErrors: Other non-OK responses throw new Error(data.reason || data.error || "Request failed with status N") with .status (HTTP status), .details, and .decision (full body) attached. Non-JSON error bodies (gateway 502/504/413/429 pages) are parsed defensively to {} so the status-bearing error still throws instead of a SyntaxError.
errorHandling.timeouts: waitForApproval throws a plain Error("Approval timeout after Nms") after options.timeout (default 300000 ms). waitForPairing throws on expiry/timeout.

package.transportNotes: waitForApproval prefers an SSE connection to GET /api/stream (event action.updated scoped to the actionId) and falls back to HTTP polling of GET /api/actions/:id every interval ms (default 5000). Query params with undefined/null values are skipped (never serialized as literal "undefined").

helperExports.scrubAct: Pure function (also applied automatically before any act payload is sent): returns a scrubbed deep copy of an act payload — drops Authorization/Cookie/x-api-key headers and masks common credential token shapes and password=/token=/secret= substrings in command/statement/body_excerpt/content_excerpt. Exported for unit testing; server still re-redacts (defense in depth).

package.relatedPackagesNotInThisInventory: @dashclaw/cli (terminal approvals, doctor, env injection), @dashclaw/mcp-server (17 MCP tools / 3 resources), @dashclaw/openclaw-plugin, @dashclaw/governance skill. Server-side agent-runtime route families (handoffs, operator secrets metadata, skill scan, posture) are deliberately NOT exposed as claw.* methods.

items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface

items.name: client.runGoverned
items.statusEvidence: no explicit marker, method is unremarkable core surface
items.purpose: One-call full governance loop: guard (with act) then createAction, then waitForApproval if pending_approval and wait!==false, then run fn(), then report a one-shot completed/failed outcome. The recommended entry point for governing a single unit of work end-to-end.

inputs.act: object, required — { kind: 'shell'|'http'|'sql'|'file', ... } evidence payload; scrubbed client-side via scrubAct before send
inputs.params: object, optional — context/action fields (action_type, declared_goal, risk_score, ...); `wait` (default true) controls whether to block on pending approval

items.response: whatever fn() resolves to
items.endpoint: N/A (local helper, no HTTP call) — internally calls POST /api/guard, POST /api/actions, GET/SSE /api/actions/:id (via waitForApproval), and POST /api/actions/:id/outcome
items.gotchas: Throws GuardBlockedError immediately if guard() returns decision:'block' (createAction is never called in that case). If fn() throws, reportActionOutcome is called with status:'failed' and the error message, then the original error is re-thrown. Passing wait:false skips waitForApproval — caller must poll separately.

DashClawError.purpose: Base error for all SDK-raised exceptions; carries .status (HTTP status int or None) and .details (parsed error body or None).
DashClawError.raised_by: _raise_normalized_http_error - translates any non-Guard/Approval HTTPError into this, attaching status + parsed JSON body as details.

GuardBlockedError.purpose: Raised when a guard decision is 'block' (run_governed) or when the server's HTTP error body indicates a guard block. Exposes .decision, .reasons, .warnings, .matched_policies, .risk_score pulled from the decision dict. status is hardcoded 403.
GuardBlockedError.raised_by: run_governed() directly on decision['decision']=='block'; also via _raise_normalized_http_error for 403 responses whose body looks like a guard decision.

ApprovalDeniedError.purpose: Raised when a human operator denies a pending action, or when a pending approval expires (decision='expired'). status hardcoded 403.
ApprovalDeniedError.raised_by: wait_for_approval() / run_governed() when the approval resolves to deny or expires.

error_model.notes: No dedicated timeout/network-error class - urllib.error.URLError / socket timeouts propagate as raw Python exceptions (not wrapped in DashClawError). Only HTTPError responses go through _raise_normalized_http_error.

items.purpose: API key protecting /api/*; maps to org_default by default.

items.name: ENCRYPTION_KEY
items.purpose: 32-char string encrypting sensitive settings.

items.name: NEXTAUTH_URL
items.purpose: NextAuth base URL (default http://localhost:3000).

items.name: NEXTAUTH_SECRET
items.purpose: NextAuth signing secret, random 32-char.

items.name: DASHCLAW_LOCAL_ADMIN_PASSWORD
items.purpose: Recommended: password for local admin account, skips OAuth for solo/self-hosted use.

items.name: CRON_SECRET
items.purpose: Recommended: secret for cron endpoints (also reused for /api/hosted/cleanup); generate via openssl rand -hex 32.

items.name: DASHCLAW_MODE
items.purpose: self_host (default) | demo (read-only sandbox for dashclaw.io).

items.name: NEXT_PUBLIC_DASHCLAW_MODE
items.purpose: Client-visible mirror of DASHCLAW_MODE.

items.name: DASHCLAW_DB_DRIVER
items.purpose: Force 'postgres' (TCP) or 'neon' (serverless); auto-detected by default.

items.name: DASHCLAW_API_KEY_ORG
items.purpose: Override which org DASHCLAW_API_KEY maps to (default org_default).

items.name: ALLOWED_ORIGIN
items.purpose: Restrict CORS to your deployment domain.

items.name: DASHCLAW_INTERNAL_BASE_URL
items.purpose: Self-host TCP Postgres only: internal key-resolution route base (default loopback on PORT); never a third-party host.

items.name: TRUST_PROXY
items.purpose: Trust x-forwarded-for from a reverse proxy for rate limiting.

items.name: PORT
items.purpose: HTTP port, default 3000.

items.name: UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL / UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN
items.purpose: Distributed rate limiting for multi-instance deploys.

items.name: DASHCLAW_DISABLE_RATE_LIMIT / DASHCLAW_RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS / DASHCLAW_RATE_LIMIT_MAX
items.purpose: Per-IP in-memory rate limit tuning, single-instance.

items.name: WEBHOOK_ALLOWED_DOMAINS
items.purpose: SSRF protection allow-list, comma-separated trusted webhook domains.

items.name: DASHCLAW_ALLOWED_ISSUER / DASHCLAW_JWT_AUDIENCE
items.purpose: Phase 2 JWT identity verification (JWKS). Required to enable bearer-token verified identity (fail-closed since v3.7 -- no issuer means bearer tokens never reach 'verified').

items.name: DASHCLAW_JTI_REPLAY_PROTECTION
items.purpose: off | best_effort | required (default). Replay protection for verified JWTs carrying a jti claim; never touches API-key callers.

items.name: DASHCLAW_JTI_MAX_TTL_SECONDS
items.purpose: Max JWT exp lifetime accepted (default 86400/24h) so the replay seen-set doesn't grow unbounded.

items.name: DASHCLAW_ACT_BINDING / DASHCLAW_ACT_BINDING_TYP
items.purpose: off | best_effort (default) | required. Binds a verified token to one (action,target,goal) tuple via an act-binding claim.

items.name: DASHCLAW_EXPOSE_ERROR_DETAIL
items.purpose: In production, redacts exception detail from API error responses unless set true.

items.name: DASHCLAW_SIGNING_KEY_JWK
items.purpose: Ed25519 private JWK for proof receipts/signed exports. Leave unset for zero-config auto-generated key stored in server_signing_keys table; public key published at /.well-known/jwks.json regardless.

items.name: REALTIME_BACKEND / REDIS_URL / REALTIME_REPLAY_WINDOW_SECONDS / REALTIME_REPLAY_MAX_EVENTS / REALTIME_ENFORCE_REDIS
items.purpose: memory (default, single-instance) | redis (cross-instance pub/sub) realtime backend config.

items.purpose: GitHub OAuth app credentials.

items.purpose: Google OAuth credentials.

items.name: ENFORCE_AGENT_SIGNATURES
items.purpose: Require signed agent actions; true by default in production.

items.name: DASHCLAW_CLOSED_ENROLLMENT
items.purpose: Require agents to be pre-registered before submitting actions.

items.name: DASHCLAW_PAIRING_TTL_MINUTES
items.purpose: Minutes before a pairing request expires (default 15).

items.name: DISABLE_PROMPT_INJECTION_SCAN
items.purpose: Prompt-injection scanning runs on every guard eval by default; set true to disable (security-relevant, leave unset).

items.name: DASHCLAW_GUARD_FALLBACK
items.purpose: require_approval (default, fail closed) | allow (self-hoster escape hatch) | block (strictest). What the guard returns when it cannot complete an evaluation (webhook timeout, semantic LLM failure, deadline exceeded).

items.name: DASHCLAW_GUARD_DEADLINE_MS
items.purpose: Policy-evaluation deadline in ms (default 3500); hooks give the whole guard call 5s with zero retries, keep this under that.

items.name: DASHCLAW_DB_POOL_MAX
items.purpose: Postgres pool max connections (default 10).

items.name: AGENT_ONLINE_WINDOW_MS
items.purpose: ms an agent counts 'online' since last heartbeat (default 120000).

items.name: GUARD_WEBHOOK_SECRET
items.purpose: HMAC secret for outbound guard webhook signing.

items.name: DASHCLAW_INTERRUPT_BUDGET / DASHCLAW_INTERRUPT_WINDOW_MIN / DASHCLAW_INTERRUPT_BUDGET_FLEET
items.purpose: Approval-interrupt flood-collapse budgets (per policy per window, and fleet-wide).

items.name: DASHCLAW_DIGEST_INTERVAL_HOURS
items.purpose: Fleet digest cadence in hours (default 24, 0 disables); needs a notification adapter configured.
